query: The Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy forms several primary non-eutectic phases during solidification and exhibits a complex, multistep crystallization sequence. Under rapid cooling, slower cooling, and subsequent reheating assessed by thermal analysis, what single intervention could increase amorphous retention and thermal stability while overcoming extensive primary crystallization? State one hypothesis containing the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted outcome relative to the alloy’s reported glass formation and crystallization behavior, the relevant cooling-rate and reheating boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: A high-purity B2O3-based fluxing treatment of the molten Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy, applied prior to casting or rapid solidification, will reduce heterogeneous nucleation sites and inhibit the formation of multiple primary non‐eutectic crystalline phases, thereby increasing amorphous phase retention and enhancing the alloy’s thermal stability during both rapid and slower cooling, as well as during subsequent reheating.
generation.material_initial_state: Molten Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy containing typical oxide inclusions and other heterogeneities that act as nucleation sites for primary crystallization.
generation.intervention: High-purity B2O3-based fluxing treatment of the molten alloy executed by adding a controlled flux-to-alloy ratio and holding the melt at 50–100 K above the liquidus temperature.
generation.conditions: The fluxing treatment is applied prior to casting/rapid solidification and is then subjected to a spectrum of cooling rates ranging from slow cooling (≈52 K/s) to rapid quenching (10^5–10^6 K/s) followed by controlled reheating for thermal analysis.
generation.structural_mediator: Reduction of surface oxide inclusions and heterogeneous nucleation centers within the melt.
generation.mechanism: The B2O3 flux effectively reacts with and removes oxygen and other impurities that form stable oxides, lowering the density of nucleation sites. This suppression of early crystal nucleation delays the onset of primary crystallization, thereby promoting a greater extent of undercooling and amorphous retention during rapid and moderate cooling, as well as an increase in the crystallization onset temperature during reheating.
generation.predicted_outcome: Flux-treated alloys will exhibit increased amorphous phase fraction and enhanced thermal stability, as signified by a delayed crystallization onset (higher onset temperature) in DSC measurements compared to non-fluxed alloys under identical cooling and reheating protocols.
generation.baseline: The reported behavior of the untreated Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy shows extensive primary crystallization, with multiple non-eutectic crystalline phases forming during slow cooling and reheating despite rapid cooling achieving amorphization.
generation.boundary: The intervention is expected to be effective within the processing window where the melt is held at 50–100 K above the liquidus temperature and under cooling rates from slow cooling (≈52 K/s) to very rapid quenching (10^5–10^6 K/s), with reheating profiles similar to those used in the reported thermal analyses.
generation.uncertainty: The magnitude of improvement in amorphous retention and delay in crystallization onset is sensitive to the flux purity, exact flux-to-alloy ratio, and hold time. There may also be unanticipated interactions between phosphorus and the flux that could affect the kinetics of phase transformation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two batches of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy: one undergoing the high-purity B2O3 fluxing treatment (using the specified flux-to-alloy ratio and holding the melt 50–100 K above the liquidus) and a control group without fluxing. Subject both batches to identical thermal processing including rapid cooling (melt-spinning, 10^5–10^6 K/s), slower cooling (≈52 K/s), and subsequent controlled reheating.
measurements: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) to determine the onset temperature of crystallization and quantify the heat flow associated with phase transformations.
X-ray diffraction (XRD) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) to identify and quantify the amorphous phase fraction versus crystalline phases.
Thermographic analysis to evaluate cooling dynamics and transformation temperatures.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the flux-treated samples do not show a statistically significant increase in amorphous phase fraction and a delayed onset of crystallization (i.e., a higher crystallization onset temperature in DSC measurements) compared to the control group under identical processing conditions, then the hypothesis that fluxing improves amorphous retention and thermal stability in this alloy is falsified.

Cooling rates significantly influence the microstructure and phase composition of the Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy. Slow cooling after arc melting results in a complex microstructure comprising multiple crystalline phases such as FCC “A”, tetragonal “B”, “C”, “D”, and orthorhombic “E”, while faster cooling after a short electric arc pulse reduces the number of phases to primarily FCC “A” and tetragonal “D”. Very rapid cooling using the melt-spinning method results in an amorphous structure, as confirmed by XRD and TEM analyses. Phosphorus addition enhances the alloy’s glass-forming ability during rapid cooling. The amorphous structure observed in the melt-spun ribbon demonstrates that the combination of phosphorus and high mixing entropy promotes the formation of amorphous phases during extremely fast cooling. decision.trend: Early work on high-entropy and amorphous alloys demonstrated that many multicomponent systems (including FeCoNiB- and P-containing alloys) are prone to partial or primary crystallization when cooled or reheated (PMC6416621, PMC7516748). Efforts to suppress unwanted phases have shown that rapid cooling (e.g., melt spinning) or containerless methods can extend undercooling and drive glass formation, but residual heterogeneous nucleation sites often remain problematic. More recently, direct thermal and microstructural analysis of the Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy (PMC11642357) revealed that even accelerated cooling and subsequent reheating can lead to early-stage primary crystallization of multiple non-eutectic phases, highlighting the persistent challenge of controlling extensive primary crystallization in this P-containing high-entropy alloy.
decision.unsolved: Despite partial success in forming amorphous structures at high cooling rates, it remains difficult to prevent extensive primary crystallization in the Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 system during slower cooling or upon reheating, limiting the alloy’s usable processing and application windows. A practical route to minimize heterogeneous nucleation and boost thermal stability under varied thermal conditions is still required.
decision.lever: Employ a high-purity B2O3-based fluxing treatment of the molten alloy before casting or rapid solidification, carefully controlling flux-to-alloy ratio, flux purity, and hold time at 50–100 K above the liquidus to eliminate oxide inclusions and reduce nucleant density.
decision.why: Fluxing is a proven method in bulk metallic glass processing to remove oxygen and other heterogeneities that seed primary phases. By minimizing these nucleation sites, the alloy can maintain an undercooled melt more effectively under rapid and moderate cooling rates, facilitating a higher fraction of amorphous content. Upon reheating, the reduced density of stable nuclei is expected to increase the onset temperature of crystallization, enhancing thermal stability. Prior studies (PMC11642357) show that eliminating early crystal nucleation is critical for achieving robust glass formation, and fluxing methods have demonstrated success in other multicomponent systems (e.g., PMC6416621, PMC7516748). A decisive test would involve comparing thermophysical characterization (e.g., DSC, TTT curves) of fluxed versus non-fluxed alloys under identical cooling and reheating cycles, verifying improved amorphous phase retention and delayed primary crystallization.
